sources.title: Siegfried M. Rump, Verification methods: Rigorous results using floating-point arithmetic, Acta Numerica 19 (2010)
sources.locator: Full 163-page article; §4.2; §§5.1–5.5; §§10.5–10.6; §10.10. The interval arithmetic definitions and verification arguments in §§5.1–5.5, the verified linear-system residual route in §10.5, and the Krawczyk inclusion discussion in §10.6 were inspected. The §10.10 determinant routine is LU/Gershgorin based, unlike the local Leibniz enclosure.

contents.name: §§4.2 and 5.1–5.5: interval enclosures, directed outward operations, and inclusion-sound expression evaluation
§10.5: an approximate inverse, a Neumann defect bound, and a residual enclosure for a verified linear solve
§10.6: Krawczyk-type set inclusion for existence and contraction-based uniqueness
§10.10: a verified determinant enclosure based on preconditioned LU and Gershgorin bounds
contents.reason: The local determinant certifier evaluates the finite Leibniz expression and proves its own interval soundness. Rump's different LU/Gershgorin algorithm is not presented as the proof or implementation of this carrier.

§5.6: Hermitian inertia and LDL context for the locally proved two-by-two determinant/trace sign test
